questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I thought it would be exciting to live in Italy considering the culture, food, weather etc. The courses at University of Milan was also suitable for my study programme in Copenhagen (relevant prioritized elective courses)...

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was actually quite easy, but you need to patient. You will eventually receive the information needed, but it might take some time... If you have any questions both Daniel Stokke at UCPH and Massimo at University of Milan are very helpful!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I sent some e-mails to Massimo at University of Milan. He replied quickly and was very helpful. You can also visit his office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at a Martinitt dorm. You will receive an in the spring/start summer email asking whether you want accommodation through University of Milan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Some of the accommodation options is a bit outside the city. However, I thought that Martinitt was quite OK with approx. 5 km to the university and city centre.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There are several busses from Martinitt (but no metro). Try to get an ATM card (corresponds to "Rejsekort" in Denmark) in beginning of your stay. Download the app and book an apointment to get your ATM card.

Be aware that you will most likely share a room and the kitchen can be a bit crowded at Martinitt, since all students are sharing one kitchen. However, italien people eat rather later, so just eat at "danish" time and you will be fine. It is also nice to cook and eat with the other Erasmus students at the dorm.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A week before your arrival you will receive an e-mail explaining how you register for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always e-mail Daniel Stokke at UCPH and Massimo at University of Milan.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. I didn't hear of any that didn't.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Remember to check the exam dates so you don't double book yourself. Link:
https://easystaff.divsi.unimi.it/PortaleStudenti/index.php?view=easytest&_lang=en&include=et_insegnamento
.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to understand the teachers the first few weeks because of their strong accents. Remember that you get a trial period the first few weeks where you can try courses and change if you want different courses. You also only register for the exam at the end of the semester (bit different system that in Copenhagen)...

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level varied a lot so some of the courses were a bit difficult while others were quite easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes take place in small class room and the teaching style is more like high school (gymnasium), where discussion and presentations are in focus.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Game Theory, Business History, Causal Inference and Policy Evaluation, Risk Management and Corporate Finance.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Following courses can be directly transferred to courses at UCPH and are very suitable for our study programme: 
- Game Theory => Mikro III
- Business History => Økonomisk Historie
- Causal Inference and Policy Evaluation => Applied Econometric Policy Evaluation (p)

The teacher in Risk Managament was very ambitious, but also strict. Corporate Finance was OK, but not very inspiring teaching style...

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I bought an e-Sim through Vodafone at the Duomo to get more wifi.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices is a bit lower than Copenhagen, but I also went out more and travelled more, so in the end I spent more money than at home - but it was worth it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't attend any clubs, sports, etc... I was busy doing other things.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus offer different cultural and social activities, you can attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy being a part of the Italian life and explore Milan.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other cities in Italy! I liked Bergamo, Florence, Bologna and Como.  Also try to get the cheap tickets for the Teatro alla Scala. You can also get very cheap youth tickets for museums!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Italians are very hospitable and enjoy sharing their culture. However, the language barrier can be challenging, but you will get use to it.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I liked living at a dorm to meet other Erasmus students. There are plenty of danes from Copenhagen, you will bump into, but it also nice and interesting to meet students from other countries.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Primarily the language barrier...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed all the great food, but also the more laid back approach to most things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Try to be open-minded. 
2) Remember to travel, be cultural and eat out when you have the opportunity. 
3) Maybe schedule a visit from someone at home to look forward to on more difficult days…

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get the ATM card for cheap and easy transportation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new friends I got while I was away and the academic motivation I came home with after a change in environment.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be patient and to learn that everything will work out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
